html:
The Quinnipiac were an Algonquian-speaking people of the coast of what is now Connecticut, along the Quinnipiac River. Their main village stood where New Haven is today.

Weakened by epidemics and under pressure from the Mohegan, Pequot and Mohawk, they sold most of their land in 1638 to English Puritans who founded the New Haven Colony. In return the English set aside a small tract for them, often called one of the first Indian reservations in the English colonies. Their numbers kept falling, and by the 1800s the survivors had joined other communities. Quinnipiac University is named after them. Nearby lived the Narragansett.
sum: The Quinnipiac were an Algonquian-speaking people of the coast of what is now Connecticut, along the Quinnipiac River. Their main village stood where New Haven is today.
